thread:
elaine (Acme): Hey @support — after today's pinned model swap our embeddings started failing. Previously vectors were length 1536, now responses show 2048 and our FAISS index throws shape errors. Anyone seen this?

emma (support): hi @elaine — ouch. Can you paste the exact request + model param you used? Also which pinned variant did you pin to? :eyes:

elaine (Acme): Request snippet:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"acme/embed-alias:v2-pinned","input":"test string"}'
```
Response excerpt:
```json
{"data":[{"embedding":[0.0123,-0.0045,0.0012,...(truncated)]}]}
```
We expected length 1536. This started after we locked the alias to a pinned variant yesterday evening.

devin (ml-eng): @emma @elaine can you share the dashboard model id (the version string) and the alias name? Also any canary notes from the onboarding?

elaine (Acme): Dashboard shows model id: embed-fast-2@2026-03-16-rc, alias is acme/embed-alias (pinned to that id). Rolling back the pin still returns 2048 embeddings. Our ingestion pipeline asserts vec.length == 1536 and is failing.

emma (support): thanks. Can you dump the first 10 values and the length header from the client? just to be sure it's not an off-by-one in your side.

elaine (Acme): pasted first 10 values: [0.0123, -0.0045, 0.0012, -0.0009, 0.021, ...] — our client reports length: 2048. Confirmed on two separate requests and two regions.

oliver (infra): I see a recent onboarding for embed-fast-2: that variant changed the base embedding dimension to 2048 (different architecture). It looks like the alias swap happened during pin creation and the alias started resolving to a mismatched-dim model. There was no guard in the alias pin flow to check embed_dim compatibility.

devin (ml-eng): confirmed. Root cause: alias pinning accepted a model version whose embedding_dim differs from the alias historical vector size. Our alias resolution code didn't validate embedding metadata. We've reproduced locally by pinning an alias to a new variant.

devin (ml-eng): Quick repro steps we used:
```bash
# create alias pointing to old model (1536)
curl -X POST /v1/models/aliases -d '{"alias":"test/alias","target":"embed-old@2025-10-01"}'
# pin alias to new model (2048)
curl -X POST /v1/models/pins -d '{"alias":"test/alias","target":"embed-fast-2@2026-03-16-rc"}'
# request embeddings -> length 2048
```
No validation error raised.

emma (support): Proposed immediate mitigations:
- Re-pin the alias to the previous 1536 model id (explicit version).
- Or call embeddings with exact model version instead of alias (model param).
- We're going to push a hotfix to validate embed_dim on pin.

oliver (infra): I've rolled the alias back for Acme at 1742110200 and it's visible in the audit log. Please test.

elaine (Acme): Confirming after the rollback our embeddings are back to length=1536, index insert passes. Thank you so much!

devin (ml-eng): We're shipping a hotfix that enforces embedding_dim compatibility when pinning an alias and surface the embedding_dim in the Model List API + console. Also adding a warning dialog in the console when pinning across dims. Ticket RNW-4531 opened and assigned to me for follow-ups.

emma (support): RNW-4531 created and escalated to enterprise ops. Action items:
- dev team to add validation + UI warning (devin)
- infra to scan recent pins and flag mismatches (oliver)
- support to notify any customers with alias pins that cross dims (emma)

deploy-bot: v1.0.3-hotfix (alias-dim-guard) deployed to canary -> rollout started.

elaine (Acme): All good on our end, pipeline green. Please loop us in on the notification. Much appreciated. :thumbsup:
